card.name: Narrator addressing reader mid-sentence
card.fires_on: Short words right after a narrator's "I", "you" or "now" in informal web explanations, such as "I hope", "You see where", "You should". The marked word is often a verb or adverb in the narrator's direct address to the reader.

modes.label: Narrator's I statements
modes.description: Verb or contraction right after "I" when the writer comments on their own explanation or method.
modes.example: I<< hope>> that made things a little clearer.

modes.label: Addressing the reader
modes.description: Word after "you" or a sentence-opening adverb in a passage speaking directly to the reader.

modes.label: Now and suddenly
modes.description: Time words like "now" or "Suddenly" that mark a shift in the story or a rhetorical question.
modes.example: Does that ring a bell<< now>>?

card.writes: It slightly suppresses words like "afterwards" and promotes "increasingly" and Chinese "越来越", with no coherent link to this pattern.
card.plain: It fires on small words in a writer's chatty asides to the reader, like "I hope" or "you should".
